question_text: Why do LSM-tree storage engines (e.g. RocksDB, Cassandra) typically outperform B-trees on write-heavy workloads?

options.text: They perform in-place updates directly on disk blocks
They append writes sequentially to an in-memory MemTable and Write-Ahead Log, avoiding random disk I/O
They eliminate disk storage by using RAM only

answer_explanation: LSM-trees convert random writes into sequential appends in memory (MemTable) and sequential WAL writes, flushing ordered SSTables to disk without random disk seek overhead.
reference_solution: Correct Choice: B. Rationale: LSM-trees convert random writes into sequential appends in memory (MemTable) and sequential WAL writes, flushing ordered SSTables to disk without random disk seek overhead.
